title: Automation Latency (Trigger to Action)
dataSources: Home Assistant state/logbook events (`homeassistant:event`), Homey flow/insights (`homey:flow`), SmartThings events (`smartthings:event`), Node-RED flow events (`nodered:event`).
app: Home Assistant / Homey / SmartThings / Hubitat / openHAB event streams via MQTT, webhooks, and REST — forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=homeassistant:event event_type=automation_triggered
| eval latency_ms=action_time*1000-trigger_time*1000
| stats avg(latency_ms) as avg_ms, p95(latency_ms) as p95_ms by automation
| where p95_ms>2000
| sort - p95_ms
description: Measures the delay between an automation being triggered and its action completing, flagging the sluggish ones that make your home feel laggy.
value: A light that takes two seconds to react feels broken; measuring automation latency finds the slow flows worth optimising.
implementation: Forward automations with trigger and action timestamps; schedule daily and tune the slowest automations.
grandmaExplanation: It measures how long your home takes to react after something triggers it, so you can fix the slow, laggy routines.
